messages.subject: MQM interval
parts:
Hi Karl,

I have read that how confidence interval behaves in MQM is not well understood but since I'm reporting an interval a little odd in a paper, I still want to understand why.

I used MQM to map a linkage group where I have detected two linked QTL roughly 25 cM apart. When I tried to estimate the 1.5-LOD confidence interval for one of the two QTL, the actual interval I got was much wider than 1.5-LOD (it's 4 and 8 lod drop on each side). I then checked the old profile at all marker and I can see markers closer to the peak location that are 1 or 3 lod drop from the peak on the right but the program seems to ignore these markers and went for markers further out. There was a slight increase for 2 lod after the immediate markers that are 1-lod or 3-lod drop from the peak and after this small rise the lod score drops continuously. Is that small rise why R/tl chose to bypass the closest 1.5-lod drop marker and went for the further one? In this case, do you suggest to follow the R/qtl output or to manually adjust the interval to be closer to the peak? 

> lodint(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.refine2.02,qtl.index=2)
           chr  pos      lod
c5.loc26.8   5 26.8 131.2664
c5.loc27     5 27.0 135.8998
c5.loc27.6   5 27.6 127.9423

Many thanks!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MQM interval
parts:
Yes, the intervals take the regions where the LOD score is within 1.5 of the peak and then turn them into a single connected interval. So if the LOD goes down a bit and then back up, you’ll get the wider interval. I would stick with this rather than exclude the larger region.

I think the reason interval ends up dropping 4 and 8 in LOD is that we calculate the endpoints only at discrete positions, and the LOD scores I likely dropping rapidly. Check that if you move one pseudomarker interior, you get LOD difference from the maximum of < 1.5.

karl
